1.note: This **day** is the day that Exodus 40:17 refers to, which is the first day of the first month of the second year. That means that this **day** occurred before the day that [1:1](ta:01) refers to, which is the first day of the second month of the second year. If it is helpful in your language, you might want to make it clear that the account that starts in this verse happened before the events in chapters 1–6. Alternate translation: [Now previously, on the day of Moses finishing]

The implication is that Moses and the Levites did all the work of setting up the sacred tent, though the text only mentions **Moses finishing**. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Moses and the Levites finishing]

1.q: וַ⁠יִּמְשַׁ֨ח אֹת֜⁠וֹ וַ⁠יְקַדֵּ֤שׁ אֹת⁠וֹ֙ וְ⁠אֶת־כָּל־כֵּלָ֔י⁠ו וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠מִּזְבֵּ֖חַ וְ⁠אֶת־כָּל־כֵּלָ֑י⁠ו וַ⁠יִּמְשָׁחֵ֖⁠ם וַ⁠יְקַדֵּ֥שׁ אֹתָֽ⁠ם
1.note: It might seem that the expression **And he anointed them, and he consecrated them** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [that he anointed and consecrated it and all its vessels and the altar and all its vessels]

2.note: Here, the author is speaking of the leaders or rulers of the houses of their fathers as if they were **the heads** of those families. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the rulers of the houses]
See how you translated the similar phrase in 1:2. Alternate translation: [the family groups of their ancestors]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. The verb **presented** needs an object to make clear what they presented. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [presented an offering]

Here, the author is speaking of the leaders as if they were **standing over** the people they supervised. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the ones who oversaw]

As the first note to [7:1](ta:07) makes clear, the events in this chapter happened before the census in chapters 1–2. So, these people have not yet been **counted**. If it is helpful in your language, you might want to make it clear that the counting happened after the events in this chapter. Alternate translation: [the ones who would be counted]

The expression **the counted ones** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. See how you translated the similar phrase in 2:4. Alternate translation: [the ones whom they, Moses, and Aaron counted]

3.note: In this verse, the word **offering** is singular in form, but it refers to all the gifts from the leaders as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “offering.” Alternate translation: [their offerings]
Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

A **covered wagon** is a kind of cart with a protective covering over it. If your readers would not be familiar with what a covered wagon is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [carts with coverings … a cart]

Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of the Dwelling. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before the Dwelling]

4.note: Here, the word **saying** introduces a direct quotation. See how you translated **saying** in [1:1](ta:01).

5.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Take the wagons and cattle from with them]

Here, just as in Numbers 4, the words **serve** and **service** refer to tasks of setting up, taking down, and carrying the sacred tent. See how you translated these words in 4:30. Alternate translation: [for the physical labor required to move]

The phrase **to serve the service** is poetic language in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to serve]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [as the tent of meeting needs to be served]

In some languages it is more natural to express **a man** with a distributive form meaning “each man” or “each one.” This refers to how Moses was to distribute the carts and oxen to each of the groups of Levites according to their needs. If your language has a distributive form, you may want to use it here. Alternate translation: [each man]

Yahweh is using the expression **according to the mouth of his service** as a common expression of his culture to mean “according to how he was required to serve.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [according to how he was required to serve]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how he serves]

7.note: This is the first of many times in this chapter that the author uses the phrase **the sons of** followed by a tribe or clan name to refer to the men who belong to that tribe or clan. See the chapter introduction for more information.

The author is using **according to the mouth of their service** as a common expression of his culture to mean “according to how they were required to serve.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in 7:5. Alternate translation: [according to how they were required to serve]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how they serve]

8.note: See how you translated this phrase in 7:7.

Here, the author means that both the **sons of Merari** and the “sons of Gershon” (7:7) are **in the hand of Ithamar**. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [their service. The service of the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari was in the hand of Ithamar]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how they serve]

The author is using **in the hand of** as a common expression of his culture to mean “under the control of” or “under the supervision of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated this phrase in 4:28. Alternate translation: [under the control of Ithamar]

9.q: וְ⁠לִ⁠בְנֵ֥י קְהָ֖ת לֹ֣א נָתָ֑ן כִּֽי־עֲבֹדַ֤ת הַ⁠קֹּ֨דֶשׁ֙ עֲלֵ⁠הֶ֔ם
9.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [But the service of the holy place was upon the sons of Kohath, so he did not give to them]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. In **he did not give**, he does not say what Moses did not give to the Kohathites. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [he did not give any wagons or cattle]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [serving]

Here, **the holy place** represents the sacred items that were kept in the holy place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the things in the holy place]

Here, the author is speaking of the responsibility of caring for the holy items as if it were a physical burden that **was upon** the Kohathites. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [was their duty]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [They carried the holy things]

The author is not referring to a specific **shoulder**. He means their shoulders in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [on their shoulders]

10.note: Here, **dedication** represents the gifts and offerings that were given to dedicate the altar. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the dedication offerings for the altar]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **dedication**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what they offered for when the altar was dedicated]

The expression **its being anointed** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Moses. Alternate translation: [Moses anointing it]

The author is using a construction in which a verb (**presented**) and its object (**offering**) come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [And the leaders gave their offering]

The term **their offering** refers to the combined gifts from all the leaders, even though each leader brought his own individual offering. The author describes it as a single collective offering, though the next verse clarifies that the leaders presented their offerings one at a time over several days. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use the plural form to emphasize that there were multiple individual offerings. Alternate translation: [their offerings]

Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of the altar. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in front of the altar]

11.q: נָשִׂ֨יא אֶחָ֜ד לַ⁠יּ֗וֹם נָשִׂ֤יא אֶחָד֙ לַ⁠יּ֔וֹם
11.note: Yahweh is using **One leader for the day, one leader for the day** as a common expression of his culture to mean “one leader on each separate day in sequence.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [One leader on each day for 12 days]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb (**present**) and its object (**offering**) come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [they shall give their offering]

In this verse, the word **offering** is singular in form, but it refers to the offerings of all the leaders of Israel as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “offering.” Alternate translation: [their offerings]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **dedication**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for when the altar is dedicated]

12.note: The author is using a construction in which a verb (**presenting**) and its object (**offering**) come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [And the one giving his offering]
If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **on the first day**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [on day one]
For these and the other names in this chapter, translate them as you did in chapter 1. See the chapter introduction for more information.

13.note: A **silver dish** is a kind of large bowl made out of silver, although its exact shape is uncertain. If your readers would not be familiar with what a **silver dish** is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [one deep silver bowl]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply “shekels” from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [its weight was 130 shekels]

These 130 **shekels** came to about one and one-half kilograms or about three and one-third pounds of silver. In your translation, you could use the ancient measurement and spell the word “shekel” the way it sounds in your language. You could also use the metric measurement given in the UST or use the measurement that your language and culture customarily use. Alternatively, you could use the ancient measurement and put a modern measurement in parentheses in the text or in a footnote.

A **silver basin** is a kind of jug or deep bowl used to store liquids, although its exact shape is uncertain. If your readers would not be familiar with what a **silver basin** is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [one silver pitcher]

These **70 shekels** came to about 800 grams or about 1.75 pounds of silver. In your translation, you could use the ancient measurement and spell the word “shekel” the way it sounds in your language. You could also use the metric measurement given in the UST or use the measurement that your language and culture customarily use. Alternatively, you could use the ancient measurement and put a modern measurement in parentheses in the text or in a footnote

The author is using the possessive form to describe a **shekel** that was used in **the holy place**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. See the chapter introduction for more information about this **shekel**. Alternate translation: [in the shekel that is used in the holy place]

The expression **full of flour mixed with the oil** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the two of which he had filled with flour that he had mixed with the oil]

The author is not referring to a specific **oil**. He means oil in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [with oil]

14.note: A **palm-sized bowl** is a kind of small ceremonial dish about the size of a person’s palm, although its exact shape is uncertain. If your readers would not be familiar with what a palm-sized bowl is, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. Alternate translation: [one large spoon]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. Here **ten gold** means “ten shekels of gold,” which the author has shortened. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [ten gold shekels]

These **ten gold** shekels came to about 114 grams or a quarter pound of gold. In your translation, you could use the ancient measurement and spell the word “shekel” the way it sounds in your language. You could also use the metric measurement given in the UST or use the measurement that your language and culture customarily use. Alternatively, you could use the ancient measurement and put a modern measurement in parentheses in the text or in a footnote.

The expression **full of incense** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that he had filled with incense]

15.note: Here, the author uses the phrase **son of cattle** to indicate that the bull was young. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a young one]

Here, the author is speaking of a male lamb as if it were a **son of his year**, meaning it was one year old. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated this phrase in 6:12. Alternate translation: [a year old]

The author implies that all three animals were used for the **burnt offering**. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [his year), all three for a burnt offering]

16.note: The author is using the possessive form to describe a **buck** that is characterized by being **of the goats**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a goat that is a buck] or [an adult male goat]

17.note: The author is using the possessive form to describe a **sacrifice** that is part of the **peace offering**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and for the animal sacrifices that are part of the peace offering]

Here, the author is speaking as if the lambs were actually **sons of a year**. This expression means that they were one year old. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in 7:15. Alternate translation: [each a year old]

18.note: If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **the second day**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [On day two]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [presented his offering]

19.note: It might seem that the expression **He presented his offering** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language since 7:18 already states that Nethanel presented. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [This was his offering]

Here the author is using a construction in which a verb (**presented**) and its object (**offering**) come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [He gave his offering]

19.q: קַֽעֲרַת־כֶּ֣סֶף אַחַ֗ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים וּ⁠מֵאָה֮ מִשְׁקָלָ⁠הּ֒ מִזְרָ֤ק אֶחָד֙ כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁבְעִ֥ים שֶׁ֖קֶל בְּ⁠שֶׁ֣קֶל הַ⁠קֹּ֑דֶשׁ שְׁנֵי⁠הֶ֣ם ׀ מְלֵאִ֗ים סֹ֛לֶת בְּלוּלָ֥ה בַ⁠שֶּׁ֖מֶן לְ⁠מִנְחָֽה
19.note: See how you translated the identical words in 7:13.

20.q: כַּ֥ף אַחַ֛ת עֲשָׂרָ֥ה זָהָ֖ב מְלֵאָ֥ה קְטֹֽרֶת
20.note: This verse is identical to 7:14, so translate it the same way.

21.q: פַּ֣ר אֶחָ֞ד בֶּן־בָּקָ֗ר אַ֧יִל אֶחָ֛ד כֶּֽבֶשׂ־אֶחָ֥ד בֶּן־שְׁנָת֖⁠וֹ לְ⁠עֹלָֽה
21.note: This verse is identical to 7:15, so translate it the same way.

22.note: This verse is identical to 7:16, so translate it the same way.

23.q: וּ⁠לְ⁠זֶ֣בַח הַ⁠שְּׁלָמִים֮ בָּקָ֣ר שְׁנַיִם֒ אֵילִ֤ם חֲמִשָּׁה֙ עַתּוּדִ֣ים חֲמִשָּׁ֔ה כְּבָשִׂ֥ים בְּנֵי־שָׁנָ֖ה חֲמִשָּׁ֑ה זֶ֛ה קָרְבַּ֥ן נְתַנְאֵ֖ל בֶּן־צוּעָֽר
23.note: Besides the different names, this verse is identical to 7:17, so translate it the same way, changing only the names.

24.note: Languages have different ways of expressing ordinal numbers. The phrase **third day** uses an ordinal number. If your language does not use ordinal numbers, you could say “day three” or express this idea in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [On day three]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply the words “presented an offering” from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Eliab, the son of Helon, presented an offering]

25.q: קַֽעֲרַת־כֶּ֣סֶף אַחַ֗ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים וּ⁠מֵאָה֮ מִשְׁקָלָ⁠הּ֒ מִזְרָ֤ק אֶחָד֙ כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁבְעִ֥ים שֶׁ֖קֶל בְּ⁠שֶׁ֣קֶל הַ⁠קֹּ֑דֶשׁ שְׁנֵי⁠הֶ֣ם ׀ מְלֵאִ֗ים סֹ֛לֶת בְּלוּלָ֥ה בַ⁠שֶּׁ֖מֶן לְ⁠מִנְחָֽה
25.note: See how you translated the identical words in 7:13.

26.q: כַּ֥ף אַחַ֛ת עֲשָׂרָ֥ה זָהָ֖ב מְלֵאָ֥ה קְטֹֽרֶת
26.note: This verse is identical to 7:14, so translate it the same way.

27.q: פַּ֣ר אֶחָ֞ד בֶּן־בָּקָ֗ר אַ֧יִל אֶחָ֛ד כֶּֽבֶשׂ־אֶחָ֥ד בֶּן־שְׁנָת֖⁠וֹ לְ⁠עֹלָֽה
27.note: This verse is identical to 7:15, so translate it the same way.

28.note: This verse is identical to 7:16, so translate it the same way.

29.q: וּ⁠לְ⁠זֶ֣בַח הַ⁠שְּׁלָמִים֮ בָּקָ֣ר שְׁנַיִם֒ אֵילִ֤ם חֲמִשָּׁה֙ עַתֻּדִ֣ים חֲמִשָּׁ֔ה כְּבָשִׂ֥ים בְּנֵי־שָׁנָ֖ה חֲמִשָּׁ֑ה זֶ֛ה קָרְבַּ֥ן אֱלִיאָ֖ב בֶּן־חֵלֹֽן

30.q: בַּ⁠יּוֹם֙ הָ⁠רְבִיעִ֔י נָשִׂ֖יא לִ⁠בְנֵ֣י רְאוּבֵ֑ן אֱלִיצ֖וּר בֶּן־שְׁדֵיאֽוּר

31.q: קָרְבָּנ֞⁠וֹ קַֽעֲרַת־כֶּ֣סֶף אַחַ֗ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים וּ⁠מֵאָה֮ מִשְׁקָלָ⁠הּ֒ מִזְרָ֤ק אֶחָד֙ כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁבְעִ֥ים שֶׁ֖קֶל בְּ⁠שֶׁ֣קֶל הַ⁠קֹּ֑דֶשׁ שְׁנֵי⁠הֶ֣ם ׀ מְלֵאִ֗ים סֹ֛לֶת בְּלוּלָ֥ה בַ⁠שֶּׁ֖מֶן לְ⁠מִנְחָֽה

32.q: כַּ֥ף אַחַ֛ת עֲשָׂרָ֥ה זָהָ֖ב מְלֵאָ֥ה קְטֹֽרֶת

33.q: פַּ֣ר אֶחָ֞ד בֶּן־בָּקָ֗ר אַ֧יִל אֶחָ֛ד כֶּֽבֶשׂ־אֶחָ֥ד בֶּן־שְׁנָת֖⁠וֹ לְ⁠עֹלָֽה

35.q: וּ⁠לְ⁠זֶ֣בַח הַ⁠שְּׁלָמִים֮ בָּקָ֣ר שְׁנַיִם֒ אֵילִ֤ם חֲמִשָּׁה֙ עַתֻּדִ֣ים חֲמִשָּׁ֔ה כְּבָשִׂ֥ים בְּנֵֽי־שָׁנָ֖ה חֲמִשָּׁ֑ה זֶ֛ה קָרְבַּ֥ן אֱלִיצ֖וּר בֶּן־שְׁדֵיאֽוּר

85.q: שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים וּ⁠מֵאָ֗ה הַ⁠קְּעָרָ֤ה הָֽ⁠אַחַת֙ כֶּ֔סֶף וְ⁠שִׁבְעִ֖ים הַ⁠מִּזְרָ֣ק הָ⁠אֶחָ֑ד
85.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [The one silver bowl weighed 130 shekels, and the one basin weighed 70 shekels]

These 130 **shekels** came to about one and one-half kilograms or about three and one-third pounds of silver. See how you translated this weight in 7:13. In your translation, you could use the ancient measurement and spell the word “shekel” the way it sounds in your language. You could also use the metric measurement given in the UST or use the measurement that your language and culture customarily use. Alternatively, you could use the ancient measurement and put a modern measurement in parentheses in the text or in a footnote.

Here, **the one silver bowl** and **the one basin** represent each of the silver bowls and basins in general, not just two of them. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use expressions that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [each silver bowl … each basin]

These 70 **shekels** came to about four-fifths of a kilogram or 1.75 pounds of silver. See how you translated this weight in 7:13. 89.q: וּ⁠בְ⁠בֹ֨א מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵד֮ לְ⁠דַבֵּ֣ר אִתּ⁠וֹ֒ וַ⁠יִּשְׁמַ֨ע & וַ⁠יְדַבֵּ֖ר אֵלָֽי⁠ו
89.note: Here, the author could be describing: (1) a specific event that happened after the altar was anointed and the offerings were given. Alternate translation: [And then Moses went to the tent of meeting to speak with him, and he heard … And he spoke to him] (2) what Moses and Yahweh normally did once the altar was anointed and the offerings were given. Alternate translation: [And whenever Moses went to the tent of meeting to speak with him, he would hear … And he would speak to him]
The pronoun **him** refers to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [with God]

The author is using **the voice** to represent God himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. However, the author intentionally used an indirect reference to God, so use an indirect form in your language if it is possible. Alternate translation: [then he heard Yahweh speaking]

89.q: מֵ⁠עַ֤ל הַ⁠כַּפֹּ֨רֶת֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־אֲרֹ֣ן הָ⁠עֵדֻ֔ת מִ⁠בֵּ֖ין שְׁנֵ֣י הַ⁠כְּרֻבִ֑ים
89.note: The implication is that Yahweh’s voice came not only from above the atonement lid, but also specifically from the space between the two cherubs that were on top of it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [from the area above the atonement lid that is on the Box of the Testimony, which is between the two cherubs that are above the Box of the Testimony]
The pronoun **he** refers to Yahweh, while the pronoun **him** refers to Moses. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh spoke to Moses]

By **And he spoke to him**, the author means that what he describes in this verse is the way that Yahweh spoke to Moses. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [He spoke to him in that way] or [Thus he spoke to him]
